title: Unified Inference Consumption Paradigm — Product Overview and Roadmap
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

Purpose: This document defines the "Unified Inference Consumption Paradigm" (UICP) — a product-level model that unifies usage patterns, billing primitives, and operational controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. UICP is intended to reduce customer confusion, improve predictability of unit economics, and create a clear migration path between short-term experimentation and long-term committed capacity.

Audience
- Product managers and pricing owners
- Engineering teams (billing, runtime, routing)
- Customer success and sales (for contract conversations)
- Finance (forecasts and revenue recognition)

Key goals
1) Simplify: present a small set of clearly documented consumption primitives that map to typical customer journeys (prototype -> scale -> enterprise).
2) Align: ensure meter semantics are identical across hosting modes whenever feasible so product analytics and customer invoices match expectations.
3) Optimize: enable feature-level levers (routes, batching, caching) to be surfaced as cost controls customers can apply per-application.
4) Grow: create packaging that reduces friction for upgrades (e.g., credits applied toward reserved capacity).

Core concepts and definitions
- Unit primitives: token-generation-unit (TGU) and embedding-unit (EU). A TGU represents 1k generated tokens of model output (billed at model-profile rates). An EU represents 1 embedding vector invocation.
- Route: a logical endpoint customers configure that maps to a model, routing policy, and cost-slo profile (e.g., route: chat-low-latency).
- Bundle: a purchasable allocation of TGUs/EUs with attributes {term, refundable_credits, route_scoped}. Bundles may be on-demand (monthly) or committed (annual).
- Route-aware bundles: bundles tagged to one or more routes so customers can buy reservations for high-value endpoints without committing for all consumption.
- Effective price: dynamic per-call price calculated from model profile, route-level optimizations (batching, cache-hit-rate adjustment), and bundle discounts.

Illustrative billing example
- Model: open-llama-70B-qk8, baseline rate: $0.020 / TGU.
- Customer purchases a 12-month bundle: 1,000,000 TGUs for $12,500 (effective $0.0125 / TGU).
- Route optimization credit: their chat route has expected 15% KV cache hit; effective per-call cost adjusts to $0.0106 / TGU for that route.

Requirements (summary table)
| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| RQ-001 | Unified meter semantics for TGUs/EUs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private | Must | Billing | All three modes report identical token counts for identical requests within +/-1% observed variance over 7d test window |
| RQ-002 | Route-aware bundle support in billing pipeline and UI | Must | Product & Billing | Bundles can be created that are route-scoped, show remaining usage, and apply discounts on invoice lines |
| RQ-003 | Effective-price telemetry exported to Console & cost API | High | Eng Runtime | Console shows modeled vs actual spend breakdown per-request and per-route for last 30d |
| RQ-004 | Migration flow: credits conversion for upgrades from Hosted to Dedicated | High | Sales Ops | Tooling converts remaining prepaid credits into usable reservation discounts with clear audit trail |

Product capabilities (feature list)
- Consumption catalog: standardized descriptions and example invoices for each bundle type.
- Route tagging and per-route controls in Console (risk controls: max QPS, latency tier, fallback variant).
- Billing API enhancements: purchase, query balance, allocate to routes, and programmatic refunds.
- Effective price estimator: SDK endpoint that returns an estimated per-call cost given model, sequence length distribution, and route config.
- Metering reconciler: daily job to compare runtime counters with billing counters and surface anomalies >1%.

Architecture overview (high level)
- Metering pipeline: runtime -> normalized event stream (token events, embed events) -> aggregator -> reconciler -> billing ledger.
- Route-aware middleware: runtime attaches route metadata to every request that is persisted through the event stream so bundle application is deterministic.
- Price engine: standalone service that calculates effective price and exposes the estimator API to Console and SDKs.

Roadmap and milestones (timeline)
- Q1 2026: design sign-off for UICP; implement token nomenclature and small-scale test harness (owner: Eng Billing).
- Q2 2026: implement route metadata propagation in runtime and telemetry (owner: Eng Runtime).
- Q3 2026: billing pipeline changes: bundles, route-scoped discounts, and UI prototypes (owner: Eng Billing + Console).
- Q4 2026: pilot with 3 customers across SMB and mid-market for route-aware bundles; iterate on legal contract templates (owner: Sales + Customer Success).
- Q1 2027: GA with full billing export compatibility and SDK estimator (owner: Product + Eng).

Rollout plan (canary -> pilot -> GA)
1) Internal canary: enable UICP in staging and a subset of internal customers; run reconciler for two business cycles, verify variance <1.5%.
2) Customer pilot: invite 3 customers representing different personas (startup, platform team, regulated enterprise). Pilot window: 30–60 days with dedicated success engagement.
3) GA: enable self-serve purchase in Console, add documentation and migration guide, publish examples and pricing matrix.

Customer migration and support notes
- Migration path for Hosted to Dedicated: offer automated credit conversion, route export/import tooling, and a migration checklist.
- For Private deployments: offer a local price-engine release that can be run in air-gapped mode and a final reconciliation report to be uploaded to the Redwood billing service.
- Support SLAs: Sales Ops and Customer Success to own conversion disputes for the first 90 days after pilot signoff.

Success metrics and KPIs
- Reduction in pricing-related support tickets by 30% after GA.
- Average time to convert a paid Hosted customer to Dedicated reduces from 45 days to 20 days.
- Billing variance between runtime and billing ledger <1% in production for 95% of customers.
- Net revenue retention uplift via route-aware bundles for mid-market customers by 12% YoY.

Operational considerations and guardrails
- Default fallback: if route metadata is missing, fall back to tenant-level bundle application; log and alert owner team.
- Fraud detection: anomalies in token usage (spikes >10x baseline) trigger an automated hold and a billing review workflow.
- Backcompat: historical invoices continue to reference legacy unit names until archive cutoff (12 months).

Open questions and decisions to make
- Pricing alignment: should effective-price estimator consider GPU-hour equivalent to inform enterprise procurement discounts? (Decision owner: Finance).
- Refund policies: what portion of committed bundles are refundable in the first 90 days? (Decision owner: Legal + Finance).
- Private deployment reconciliation cadence: daily vs weekly for air-gapped customers? (Decision owner: Eng Private Deployments).

Next steps (action items)
- Product: finalize acceptance criteria for RQ-001..RQ-004 by 2026-11-30 (owner: Asha Patel).
- Engineering: create trackable tickets for route metadata propagation and price-engine API by 2026-12-07 (owner: Diego Marquez).
- Sales: select pilot customers and draft pilot contract template by 2027-01-15 (owner: Rina Sato).

Appendix: example CLI flows
1) Create route-aware bundle (example):
   redwood billing create-bundle --name "chat-reserve-100k" --tgus 100000 --term 12m --routes chat-low-latency --price 1250
2) Query effective price (example):
   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/cost-estimator?model=open-llama-70B-qk8&seq=512&route=chat-low-latency
